output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson) - Aria 3 recalibration, number bar sensor, battery

Last month I told Dana I would write this up once my machine had been through a real trial. It has now been through eight days of trial, so here is the review, following Ellen's pinned format.

Equipment: Stenvale Aria 3.

Shop: Harbor Point Steno Service, off York Road in Towson. It is a two-person shop, and the technician I dealt with was Gloria Ruark. Parking in back is free.

Dropped off: Monday, October 19. Picked up: Tuesday, October 27. They quoted 10 business days and I had it back in 6.

Work requested: full recalibration, number bar sensor inspection, cleaning and a firmware update. The work order was HP-4471.

Quoted: $285. Paid: $310. The extra $25 was a battery replacement. Gloria found the internal battery was holding about 60% of rated capacity and emailed me to ask before doing anything. I said yes. I paid by card at pickup, and I paid personally, as I do for all my equipment. The court does not reimburse me.

Loaner: yes, an Aria 2, issued at drop-off.

What was done: full keyboard recalibration, number bar depression sensor replaced, internal cleaning, firmware updated from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1, and the battery. The work carries a 90-day warranty. The machine came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment made. I have never gotten that from anyone, and I wish more shops did it.

How it held up: my first full day back on the Aria 3 was expert testimony from an engineer who talks almost entirely in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. That was the test I cared about, and it has held up since.

Price: $310 is fair for what was done. The thing that stood out to me was that Gloria asked before adding the battery. It is a small courtesy, but it is the difference between a shop I trust and one I watch.

The loaner: the Aria 2's tilt arm would not hold its position. It slipped in the middle of an afternoon deposition, and I propped the machine on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I told Gloria by email. She thanked me for the note and said they would repair it. It was not a big problem for me, but if you take the loaner, check the arm before you leave the shop.

The weakness is the phone. The line is staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4, and that is all. On Wednesday, October 21, I called to ask how things were going and it rang out. There was no voicemail box to leave a message in. Gloria emailed me the next day, so I did get an answer, but if you work a Monday docket, or you are in court all day Tuesday through Thursday, you will not catch them live. Email worked fine for me. I would not count on being able to call in an emergency, and I would not count on a Monday or Friday call going anywhere.

Bottom line: the work was good, the price was fair, the shop was honest, and it was done ahead of schedule. The communication is limited by those phone hours, and you should plan around that.

Dana, since you asked about this specifically: yes, I would trust them with your Aria, and your problem is the same one I had. Two things I would do. Take the shop's loaner, since you cannot be without a machine, and test its tilt arm before you leave. And when you drop yours off, ask for Gloria's email address and send your questions there, not by phone.

If anyone else has been there, please add your experience below. One visit is a small sample.

Maureen
